::: {#sol-best-discriminator}

The made-up point $G(\vecf{Z})$ has density $p_g$,
so $\E{\logf{1 - D(G(\vecf{Z}))}} = \int p_g(\vx) \logf{1 - D(\vx)} \, d\vx$.
Writing the first expectation the same way puts $V$ in one integral over $\vx$:

$$
V(D, G) = \int \paren{p(\vx) \logf{D(\vx)} + p_g(\vx) \logf{1 - D(\vx)}} \, d\vx.
$$

The integral is largest when $D(\vx)$ maximizes the integrand at each $\vx$ separately.
With $a = p(\vx)$, $b = p_g(\vx)$ and $u = D(\vx)$,
the integrand is $f(u) = a \logf{u} + b \logf{1 - u}$ on $0 < u < 1$.
For $a, b > 0$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
f'(u) &= \frac{a}{u} - \frac{b}{1 - u} && \text{(differentiate)} \\
0 &= \frac{a}{u} - \frac{b}{1 - u} && \text{(set } f'(u) = 0 \text{)} \\
0 &= a (1 - u) - b u && \text{(multiply by } u (1 - u) \text{)} \\
0 &= a - (a + b) u && \text{(collect the terms in } u \text{)} \\
u &= \frac{a}{a + b}. && \text{(solve for } u \text{)}
\end{aligned}
$$

$f''(u) = -a / u^2 - b / (1 - u)^2 < 0$,
so that $u$ is the maximum.
Where $b = 0$ the integrand increases toward $u = 1$,
and where $a = 0$ it increases toward $u = 0$;
$a / (a + b)$ gives those values too.
The best discriminator is $D(\vx) = p(\vx) / \paren{p(\vx) + p_g(\vx)}$.
Where the generator's density equals the data's,
the best discriminator is $\frac{1}{2}$.

:::
